Pregnancy: paroxetine alone is category D for cardiac malformations; lithium for Ebstein anomaly (low absolute risk); valproate strongly teratogenic; sertraline/citalopram generally considered safest SSRIs in pregnancy. Lithium narrow therapeutic index (0.6-1.2 mM target) with toxicity ≥1.5 mM — NSAIDs/ACEis/thiazides reduce renal clearance and precipitate intoxication.
sar_summary: SSRI SAR is dominated by the orthosteric SERT pocket binding pose: fluoxetine's aryloxyalkylamine, sertraline's tetralin, paroxetine's piperidine, and citalopram's phthalan — each occupies the same site with different selectivities for off-targets driven by accessory pharmacophores (paroxetine's piperidine for NET, sertraline's dichloro substitution for DAT). Atypical antipsychotic SAR balances D2 affinity against 5-HT2A:D2 ratio (the higher the ratio, the more 'atypical'); clozapine's tricyclic dibenzodiazepine scaffold with N-methylpiperazine is the prototype, with thienobenzodiazepine (olanzapine) and dibenzothiazepine (quetiapine) being scaffold-conservative successors. Aripiprazole's dichlorophenylpiperazine + quinolinone is the unique partial-agonist scaffold. MAOI SAR turns on the warhead: hydrazine (phenelzine) reduces FAD non-selectively; cyclopropylamine (tranylcypromine) opens to form a covalent adduct; propargyl (selegiline, rasagiline) provides MAO-B selectivity. Lamotrigine's phenyltriazine is sui generis as a use-dependent Na blocker, distinct from the hydantoin (phenytoin) and dibenzazepine (carbamazepine) sodium-channel-blocking scaffolds.

class_name: Serotonergic phenethylamine psychedelics (2C-x, DOx, mescaline analogues, NBOMe / NBOH / NBF / NBMD)
shared_mechanism: Primary target is the 5-HT2A receptor (Gαq-coupled), with secondary activity at 5-HT2C and 5-HT2B. Activation drives PLCβ → PIP2 hydrolysis → IP3 + DAG → intracellular Ca2+ release and PKC activation; downstream ERK1/2 phosphorylation. The cortical psychedelic effect tracks Gαq-pathway engagement rather than β-arrestin-2 recruitment (DOI-induced head-twitch is abolished in Gq-KO mice but preserved in β-arr2-KO; see PMC12491688). 5-HT2A receptor heteromerises with mGluR2 in cortex; this heteromer is implicated in the psychedelic signalling profile (Gonzalez-Maeso 2008, PMID 18297054). The N-benzyl head of NBOMe/NBOH derivatives forms an additional contact in the extracellular vestibule, locking the receptor into an active-like state — this is the structural basis of the ~100-fold potency gain over the parent 2C drug.
shared_pk_summary: Parent 2C phenethylamines (2C-B, 2C-I, 2C-E, 2C-D, etc.) are MAO-A/B substrates with high first-pass deamination; oral bioavailability is modest and intranasal increases potency ~3-fold. DOx amphetamines (DOI, DOB, DOM, DOC) are protected from MAO by the α-methyl group → longer half-life (10–30 h) and lower oral doses (1–10 mg vs 15–30 mg for the parent 2C). Mescaline analogues with bulkier 4-alkoxy groups (escaline, proscaline) are 5–8× more potent than mescaline due to lipophilicity-driven BBB penetration. NBOMe/NBOH series have very low oral bioavailability because of extensive first-pass O-demethylation (CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 dominate; CYP2D6 is responsible for ~69% of 25B-NBOMe clearance per Caspar 2018); they are dosed sublingually/buccally to bypass first-pass. Mescaline itself is NOT a CYP2D6 substrate; cleared mainly by MAO-A (TMPAA) and N-acetylation (Vizeli 2025).
shared_safety: Acute risks scale with potency. 2C-B and the parent 2C drugs have a wide therapeutic window. DOx amphetamines have a steep dose-response curve and 18–36 h duration making accidental re-dosing common. NBOMe series (especially 25I-, 25C-, 25B-NBOMe) have caused dozens of deaths from sympathomimetic toxicity: tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, seizures, multi-organ failure. Mechanism is primarily α1-adrenergic engagement plus 5-HT2A-mediated vasoconstriction. Bromo-DragonFLY combines 5-HT2A super-potency (Ki ~0.04 nM) with α1 agonism and 12–48 h duration, causing peripheral vasospasm/necrosis. 5-HT2B partial agonism across the class raises long-term cardiac valvulopathy concern with chronic use (Roth 2007, PMID 17202345). hERG data are sparse for the NBOMe series specifically but QT prolongation is reported in clinical case series.
sar_summary: 2C-x → DOx: adding an α-methyl protects from MAO, increases potency ~10× and duration ~5×. 2C-x → 25x-NBOMe: N-benzyl with 2'-methoxy increases 5-HT2A binding 14–100× (the 2'-OMe is critical; ortho-OH gives the NBOH series which is slightly less potent at 5-HT2A but is rapidly hydrolysed in vivo to the parent 2C). NBOMe → NBOH: similar 5-HT2A affinity but NBOH is metabolised faster (CYP2D6) and partly releases the parent 2C in vivo. NBOMe → NBF/NBMD: para-fluoro or methylenedioxy on the benzyl ring; comparable potency, less human data. 4-position halogen size: Br (2C-B) > I (2C-I) > Cl (2C-C) > F gives the strongest 5-HT2A binding at Br/I. 4-alkoxy (escaline series) is selective for 5-HT2C in some studies. Adding constraining rings (FLY, DragonFLY) locks the 2,5-dimethoxy groups out-of-plane and dramatically increases 5-HT2A affinity (DragonFLY > FLY > 2C-B).

class_name: Ergolines and lysergamides (LSD-family 5-HT2A agonists)
shared_mechanism: Tetracyclic ergoline scaffold acting as polypharmacology 5-HT agonists with highest potency at 5-HT2A. The diethylamide moiety (LSD) plus the ergoline rigid core enables a 'lid' interaction with ECL2 (Leu229) of the 5-HT2A orthosteric pocket, trapping the receptor in a β-arrestin-favouring conformation. Residence time on the receptor is ~3–4 hours — orders of magnitude longer than 5-HT — directly producing the long subjective duration. Pharmacology also includes potent 5-HT1A, 5-HT2C, 5-HT6, 5-HT7, D1/D2 partial agonism, and TAAR1 activity. Wacker 2017 (Cell) and Kim 2020 (Cell) crystal structures clarified the bias mechanism; Ippolito 2025 (Br J Pharmacol) reopened the debate by arguing that signalling efficacy (not bias) differentiates hallucinogenic from non-hallucinogenic 5-HT2A ligands.
shared_pk_summary: Oral bioavailability ~70–80%; Cmax 1–5 ng/mL for typical 50–200 µg doses; Tmax 1.5–2.5 h; t½ 2.5–4 h (LSD itself). Subjective duration far exceeds plasma t½ due to slow receptor dissociation. Metabolism: CYP3A4 (~30%), CYP2D6, CYP1A2, CYP2E1 (minor) — major metabolite 2-oxo-3-OH-LSD is inactive. N1-acyl prodrugs (1P-, 1cP-, 1B-, ALD-52) hydrolyse to LSD via plasma/liver carboxylesterases (CES1/2) with in-vitro t½ ~5 min; in vivo functionally equivalent to LSD.
shared_safety: Acute lethal toxicity in humans extraordinarily low (no clearly documented overdose deaths from pure LSD). Main acute risks: psychological distress, hyperthermia at supratherapeutic doses (>1 mg), serotonin-syndrome risk when combined with SSRIs/MAOIs/lithium (lithium combination linked to seizures). Chronic risks: HPPD (rare), psychiatric vulnerability in predisposed individuals. Cardiovascular concern at high doses via 5-HT2B (valvulopathy) is theoretical for chronic high-frequency dosing only. hERG affinity weak (Ki ~6 μM).
sar_summary: N6-methyl → ethyl (ETH-LAD) or allyl (AL-LAD) modestly changes potency and qualitative profile; diethylamide → 2,4-dimethylazetidide (LSZ) constrains the bioactive rotamer and slightly outperforms LSD; replacement with amide (LSA) drops potency ~30× and shifts toward sedative profile via α-adrenergic. N1 acylation reduces direct 5-HT2A binding 1–2 orders of magnitude but is restored in vivo by serum esterase hydrolysis (the prodrug pattern: 1P-/1cP-/1B-LSD, ALD-52). Dihydrogenation at 9,10 (ergoloids/Hydergine) abolishes hallucinogenic activity and produces α-adrenergic blocker profile.

class_name: 4-Substituted tryptamines (psilocin/psilocybin family — 4-OH, 4-AcO, 4-PrO, 4-PO esters/ethers)
shared_mechanism: 4-Hydroxylation of the tryptamine indole confers high 5-HT2A potency with full-to-partial Gq efficacy. N-alkyl size modulates 5-HT1A vs 5-HT2A balance: small N-methyl (psilocin) gives full Emax at 5-HT2A with substantial 5-HT2C; larger N-alkyl (4-HO-MIPT, 4-HO-DET) progressively favours 5-HT2A over 5-HT2C/SERT. Per Ippolito 2025, the family shows minimal Gq-vs-arrestin bias (LSD-distinct). 4-Phosphate (psilocybin), 4-acetate (4-AcO-DMT etc), and 4-propionate (4-PrO-DMT) are prodrugs requiring intestinal/plasma hydrolysis to the active 4-OH species; the prodrug improves oral bioavailability and reduces gastric instability of the hot 4-OH phenol. Norpsilocin (no N-methyls) is more potent than psilocin at 5-HT2A in vitro BUT does not produce hallucinogenic HTR in mice — secondary-amine 4-OH compounds are BBB-restricted (Glatfelter 2022).
shared_pk_summary: Oral psilocybin bioavailability 52.7 ± 20% (as psilocin); Cmax ~19 ng/mL psilocin at 25 mg psilocybin; Tmax 1.5–2 h; t½ 2–3 h. Metabolism: dominant UGT1A10 (intestinal) + UGT1A9 (hepatic) glucuronidation (~80%) + MAO-A oxidation (~15%) → 4-HIAA; CYP2D6/3A4 minor. Protein binding ~66%. Free phenol (psilocin) chemically unstable in solution at neutral pH (autoxidation to bluish quinone).
shared_safety: Wide therapeutic index. Acute lethality essentially nil from pure compound. Main concerns: bad-trip psychological distress, transient hypertension/tachycardia, modest 5-HT2B activity giving theoretical valvulopathy risk for chronic high-frequency dosing. Drug interactions: SSRI chronic use blunts response (5-HT2A downregulation); MAOIs modestly potentiate via blocking 15% MAO-A clearance.
sar_summary: 4-position modification: 4-OH (psilocin family, active) > 4-AcO (prodrug, equivalent in vivo) > 4-PrO (slower onset prodrug) > 4-PO (psilocybin itself, the natural prodrug). N-substituents: NMe2 (psilocin, full agonist), NMeEt (4-HO-MET, similar potency), NMeiPr (4-HO-MIPT, more 2A-selective), NEt2 (4-HO-DET, Hofmann's CZ-74), NPr2 (4-HO-DPT), NiPr2 (4-HO-DiPT, unusually weak 5-HT2C). Removing both N-methyls (norpsilocin, 4-HT) destroys CNS bioavailability despite higher intrinsic potency.

class_name: 5-Methoxy-tryptamines (5-MeO-DMT family, including bufotenin)
shared_mechanism: 5-Methoxy substitution flips the 5-HT2A/5-HT1A selectivity vs the 4-OH family — 5-MeO-DMT itself is 100–1000× selective for 5-HT1A over 5-HT2A. The defining biased-agonism story: 5-MeO-DMT is G-protein biased AT 5-HT2A (favouring Gq Ca²⁺ over β-arrestin), the opposite of LSD's arrestin bias. This is thought to underlie the qualitative difference in phenomenology (ego-loss without visuals) and the absence of tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing. 5-Methoxy substitution dramatically REDUCES monoamine release potency vs unsubstituted tryptamines (αMT) and abolishes oral MAO resistance — most 5-MeO compounds require MAOI (ayahuasca) or non-oral routes to be active.
shared_pk_summary: 5-MeO-DMT vaporized: onset seconds, peak 1 min, duration 15–20 min. IM: onset 1–6 min, duration up to 60 min. Sublingual: Tmax 20 min, t½ 28 min. Insufflation (BPL-003 benzoate): Tmax 9 min, t½ 30 min. Plasma t½ very short (12–19 min) due to rapid MAO-A clearance. Metabolism: MAO-A (~70%) → 5-methoxyindole-3-acetic acid; CYP2D6 (~20%) → bufotenin (5-HO-DMT, active metabolite with ~10× higher 5-HT2A affinity). Bufotenin itself is much more BBB-limited due to 5-OH polarity.
shared_safety: Wide acute margin from pure compound but unique among classical psychedelics for blackout-amnesia at moderate doses, autonomic instability, transient unconsciousness/cataleptic state. Reports of cardiac strain at high doses. CYP2D6 inhibitor co-use (paroxetine, fluoxetine) blocks bufotenin formation. MAOI combination dangerous (serotonin syndrome).
sar_summary: N-alkyl size: small Me, Et, iPr similar. αMethyl (5-MeO-AMT) extends half-life dramatically (~16 h). Pyrrolidine N (5-MeO-PYR-T) maximises 5-HT1A selectivity. Allyl-amino derivatives (5-MeO-DALT, 5-MeO-MALT) are most 5-HT2A-preferring among 5-MeO family — opposite to most others. 5-Methoxy → 5-hydroxy (bufotenin) increases receptor affinity 10× but BBB-limits the compound. Halogenation at 4, 6, or 7 (4F-5-MeO-DMT etc) explored as SAR probes.

class_name: Simple N,N-dialkyltryptamines (DMT, DET, DPT, DIPT, MIPT, EIPT etc — no 4- or 5- ring substitution)
shared_mechanism: Tryptamine + 2 alkyls on the side-chain N. Direct moderate-affinity 5-HT2A agonists (Ki 100–500 nM range, partial-to-full Emax at Gq). Larger N-alkyls progressively block MAO-A active site, so N,N-dimethyl (DMT) needs MAOI for oral activity, N,N-diethyl (DET) is borderline orally active, N,N-dipropyl (DPT) and N,N-diisopropyl (DIPT) are orally active. Also σ1, TAAR1, weak SERT at micromolar; sigma-1 likely relevant for endogenous DMT but not exogenous recreational doses.
shared_pk_summary: DMT IV t½ 6–15 min; smoked similar. With MAOI (ayahuasca, DMT t½ extends to 4 h). DPT/DIPT SC active 30–60 min onset. Metabolism: MAO-A dominant (90% DMT); minor CYP2D6 (N-oxide, 6-OH). No CYP2D6 PM contraindication established.
shared_safety: Acute lethality nil at recreational doses. Cardiovascular: brief BP/HR spike during peak. MAOI combination danger (ayahuasca with SSRI = serotonin syndrome). No tachyphylaxis with closely spaced dosing per Strassman 1996.
sar_summary: Alkyl ladder Me<Et<Pr<iPr progressively reduces MAO-A susceptibility and shifts phenomenology (DIPT uniquely produces auditory rather than visual distortion). Asymmetric N-substitution (MIPT, EIPT) produces hybrid profiles. α-methyl substitution (αMT, αET) confers MAO resistance + dopamine release → stimulant/entactogen hybrid.

class_name: α-Alkyl tryptamines (αMT, αET and analogues — substrate-type releasers / hybrid psychedelic-stimulant)
shared_mechanism: α-Methyl (or α-ethyl) substitution sterically blocks MAO-A oxidative deamination AND converts the compound into a substrate-type SERT/NET/DAT releaser by analogy with amphetamine. Net pharmacology: full 5-HT/NE/DA release + 5-HT2A agonism + weak MAO-A inhibition. Hybrid stimulant-entactogen-psychedelic phenomenology — αMT was sold as Indopan antidepressant in USSR, αET as Monase by Upjohn (withdrawn 1962 for agranulocytosis).
shared_pk_summary: αMT oral t½ ~16 h, onset 1–2 h, duration 12–24 h. Long duration is the dominant safety risk. Metabolism CYP2D6 + partial MAO-A.
shared_safety: Multiple deaths in 2000s research-chemical wave from 5-HT-syndrome-like presentations at moderate doses (40–60 mg). 5-HT2B chronic concern (cf. fenfluramine, MDMA). Agranulocytosis idiosyncrasy reported for αET. Narrow margin between recreational and toxic dose vs other tryptamines.
sar_summary: α-methyl baseline (αMT) vs α-ethyl (αET) — longer chain reduces potency. Ring substitution (5-MeO-AMT) attenuates DA/NE release while preserving 5-HT release + 5-HT2A agonism.

class_name: β-Carbolines (harmala alkaloids — harmine, harmaline, THH)
shared_mechanism: Tricyclic β-carbolines from Peganum harmala (Syrian rue) and Banisteriopsis caapi (ayahuasca vine). Harmine and harmaline are potent, reversible, competitive MAO-A inhibitors (IC50 2–8 nM at human MAO-A, >10,000× selective over MAO-B). Mechanism enables oral DMT activity (the essence of ayahuasca). Also DYRK1A inhibition (harmine, IC50 80 nM) — significant for β-cell proliferation research; mild 5-HT2A binding; very weak SSRI activity (THH is a 3 μM SSRI).
shared_pk_summary: Harmine oral (ayahuasca) Cmax ~115 ng/mL at 250 mg, Tmax 90 min, t½ 2 h. Harmaline similar but more lipophilic (better CNS penetration). THH t½ 9 h (the lingering 'afterglow' component). Metabolism CYP1A2 + CYP2D6 → O-demethylated harmol/harmalol (active, lower potency).
shared_safety: Reversible MAO-A inhibition is safer than irreversible MAOIs (phenelzine) for tyramine interactions, but combination with SSRIs/SNRIs/triptans/other serotonergic agents → serotonin syndrome (recommend 5-week fluoxetine washout). Acute β-carboline doses produce tremor, nausea, sedation (harmaline > harmine). Pure harmine deaths essentially unreported.
sar_summary: Aromatic dihydro/tetrahydro reduction: harmine (fully aromatic, most potent MAOI) → harmaline (dihydro, more sedating) → THH (tetrahydro, weak MAOI, SSRI character). N-methylation, ring methoxylation tune potency. Banisterine = harmine (alternative name).

class_name: Endogenous tryptamines (serotonin, melatonin, 5-HTP, tryptophan, NMT, tryptamine itself)
shared_mechanism: Endogenous mammalian tryptamines/precursors. Serotonin is the reference 5-HT receptor agonist (14 subtypes). Melatonin is selective for MT1/MT2 (subnanomolar Ki). Tryptamine itself is the prototype TAAR1 agonist (EC50 110 nM) but rapidly MAO-A-cleared, so not orally psychoactive alone. 5-HTP and tryptophan are precursors: cross BBB and increase central serotonin via AADC/TPH2.
shared_pk_summary: Serotonin: not orally psychoactive (BBB impermeable). Melatonin: oral F ~15%, Tmax 40 min, t½ 45 min, CYP1A2-dominated metabolism (fluvoxamine raises AUC 17×). 5-HTP: oral F 70%, t½ 1.5–2 h, AADC-converted. Tryptophan: ~95% routed to kynurenine, only ~5% to 5-HT synthesis.
shared_safety: Generally safe in physiological/supplement doses. 5-HTP + MAOI/SSRI → serotonin syndrome. Melatonin in pregnancy and immune-suppressed populations cautious. Tryptophan EMS outbreak 1989 linked to Showa Denko contamination, not the amino acid itself.
sar_summary: Hydroxyl position determines receptor target: 5-OH (serotonin) → 5-HT receptors; 5-methoxy + N-acetyl (melatonin) → MT1/MT2; phosphorylation at 4 (psilocybin) → 4-HT prodrug system.

class_name: Triptans (5-HT1B/1D agonists — antimigraine sumatriptan family)
shared_mechanism: Selective 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D agonists. 5-HT1B activation constricts cranial vessels; 5-HT1D inhibits trigeminal sensory neuropeptide release. Antimigraine without psychedelic activity (no significant 5-HT2A binding at therapeutic concentrations). Coronary 5-HT1B activation is the main contraindication (chest pain, MI risk in CAD).
shared_pk_summary: Zolmitriptan: oral F 40%, Tmax 2 h, t½ 3 h; active CYP1A2-mediated N-desmethyl metabolite has ~2× higher 5-HT1B/D affinity than parent. Metabolism CYP1A2 (primary) + MAO-A (inactivates active metabolite).
shared_safety: FDA black-box serotonin syndrome warning with SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs (despite weak 5-HT2A activity — class-wide caution). Coronary vasospasm risk: contraindicated in CAD, uncontrolled HTN, recent MI. Medication-overuse headache with frequent use.
sar_summary: Indole or indazole core + ethylamine + sulfonamide/amide tail. Naratriptan, zolmitriptan, rizatriptan, frovatriptan, eletriptan, almotriptan, sumatriptan differ in CNS penetration, half-life, and CYP route.

class_name: Non-recreational pharmaceutical or peptide compounds (peptide hormones, kinase probes, neuropeptide ligands)
shared_mechanism: These compounds appear in the parent dataset due to indole-containing or tryptophan-containing substructure but have no recreational/psychedelic relevance. Includes GnRH agonists (buserelin, leuprolide, goserelin, nafarelin, histrelin, etc — pituitary-gonadal axis suppression for prostate cancer / endometriosis / precocious puberty); CCK-A/B receptor ligands (PD-series, BC-264, GR94800 — research probes); growth-hormone secretagogues (pralmorelin, anamorelin, examorelin, macimorelin); HDAC inhibitors (dacinostat); and miscellaneous research tool compounds.
shared_pk_summary: Highly variable by class — peptides typically require SC/IM/depot delivery, very short plasma half-life unless in depot formulation (goserelin acetate 28-day depot, leuprolide LAR 1/3/6-month).
shared_safety: Class-specific — GnRH agonists cause hypogonadism (hot flashes, bone density loss, sexual dysfunction); CCK ligands largely not approved for human use.
sar_summary: Not applicable as a psychedelic class. Included only for namespace deduplication.

class_name: Tryptophan derivatives, peptides, and metabolic intermediates
shared_mechanism: Tryptophan-based amino acids, peptides, conjugates, glucosinolates, and analytical reference standards. Not directly psychoactive. Either upstream of serotonin synthesis (free L-Trp), components of larger peptides (glycyl-tryptophan, tryptophyl-tryptophan), or chemical intermediates (Fmoc/Cbz/Boc-protected derivatives) used in peptide synthesis or as reference compounds.
shared_pk_summary: L-Tryptophan: oral, ~95% routed to kynurenine pathway, ~5% to serotonin. Peptide derivatives variable by sequence and route.
shared_safety: Generally safe; tryptophan EMS link was contaminant-specific.
sar_summary: Not applicable.

class_name: Halogenated / multiply-substituted tryptamines (lab probes, no human use)
shared_mechanism: Halogenation (F, Cl, Br) of the tryptamine indole at 4, 5, 6, or 7 produces lab probes for SAR studies of 5-HT receptor selectivity, MAO substrate properties, and SERT/SLC6A4 substrate behaviour. Examples: 5,7-dihydroxytryptamine (5,7-DHT, classical serotonergic neurotoxin), 5-bromotryptamine, 6-fluorotryptamine, 4-Br-DMT, 5-Cl-DMT. Most have not been characterised in humans and lack controlled pharmacology data.
shared_pk_summary: Unknown in humans.
shared_safety: 5,7-DHT and 5,6-DHT are documented serotonergic axon toxins (rodent stereotaxic studies). Other halogenated tryptamines lack human safety data.
sar_summary: Position 5 halogenation usually preserves 5-HT receptor affinity while altering metabolic stability. Position 4 strongly favours psychedelic activity (cf. psilocin). 5,6/5,7-dihydroxy → neurotoxin.

class_name: Generic / obscure tryptamine NPS without published pharmacology
shared_mechanism: Novel psychoactive substance tryptamines without published controlled in-vitro or human characterisation. Pharmacology is inferred from structural class (likely 5-HT2A partial agonists), but no quantitative receptor data is published.
shared_pk_summary: Unknown.
shared_safety: Unknown — extrapolated from class.
sar_summary: See parent class entries (4-OH, 5-MeO, αalkyl) depending on substitution pattern.

class_name: Amphetamine-type monoamine releasers (TAAR1 + reverse transport at DAT/NET/SERT + VMAT2 reverse transport)
shared_mechanism: Amphetamine-type stimulants act on three converging substrates: (1) they are TAAR1 full agonists, with TAAR1 activation desensitising DAT via PKA/PKC and slowing dopamine neuron firing; (2) they are substrates for DAT/NET/SERT (depending on substituent pattern), entering the cytosol and causing reverse transport ('non-exocytotic release') by reversing the Na+/Cl- electrochemical gradient the transporters normally use; (3) inside the cytosol they are weak bases that collapse the proton gradient across vesicular VMAT2, displacing monoamines from synaptic vesicles into the cytosol where they can be reverse-transported out. The relative ratio of DAT:NET:SERT substrate activity is set by ring substituents — unsubstituted/N-methyl/2-fluoro favour DA+NE, 4-halogen shifts toward SERT, 4-methylthio/4-methoxy make the compound SERT-dominant. Rothman & Baumann's synaptosomal release-assay EC50 values (PMID 11071707, PMID 18307294) are the canonical reference.
shared_pk_summary: Most amphetamines are well absorbed orally (F = 70–100%), have small-to-moderate Vd (3–6 L/kg), low protein binding (15–40%), and are eliminated by a combination of CYP2D6 hydroxylation (para-hydroxylation, then COMT/SULT), N-demethylation (CYP2D6/CYP3A4), deamination (FMO3, DBH), and direct renal excretion of unchanged drug — which is pH-dependent because the protonated amine is a tertiary base (pKa ~9.9). Acidic urine increases renal clearance (t1/2 ~7 h); alkaline urine reduces it (t1/2 >20 h). Typical half-life of d-amphetamine in adults is 9–11 h; l-amphetamine is 11–14 h; d-methamphetamine 9–12 h. The α-methyl group is what protects amphetamines from MAO degradation (versus phenethylamine itself, t1/2 ~30 s).
shared_safety: The classic acute hazards are (1) hyperthermia (multifactorial: sympathomimetic vasoconstriction limits heat dissipation, 5-HT release activates 5-HT2A-mediated thermogenesis, mitochondrial uncoupling); (2) sympathetic crisis (HTN, tachycardia, MI, stroke, aortic dissection); (3) serotonin syndrome with serotonergic releasers especially combined with MAOIs or SSRIs; (4) for 4-halogenated and 4-thio/methoxy compounds (4-MTA, PMA, 4-CA, 4-BA) — selective serotonergic axonal neurotoxicity (Fuller PMID 1196472) and 5-HT2B-mediated cardiac valvulopathy / pulmonary hypertension (Rothman/Setola, PMID 11104741, PMID 12649293). PMA/PMMA are uniquely dangerous because they combine SERT release with MAO-A inhibition (IC50 300–600 nM and 1700 nM respectively, Reyes-Parada DOI:10.3389/fphar.2019.01590) producing delayed-onset hyperthermia and serotonin syndrome (peak 4–6 h after dose rather than 1–2 h, leading to repeat dosing). Long-term — chronic high-dose methamphetamine causes DAT/SERT terminal damage detectable by PET (McCann PMID 9504281). hERG is generally not the primary cardiotoxicity mechanism for this class (in contrast to cocaine analogues). 5-HT2B is the main valve risk; fenfluramine's metabolite norfenfluramine has Ki 11–52 nM at 5-HT2B (Rothman PMID 11104741) which is why fen-phen caused valvulopathy while phen-only did not (phentermine has no 5-HT2B activity).
sar_summary: Core SAR axes for amphetamine class: (1) α-methyl is essential for oral activity (protects from MAO; bare PEA t1/2 ~30 s) and for switching from PEA's primarily MAO-substrate behaviour to monoamine release. (2) N-methyl (→ methamphetamine) increases lipophilicity, BBB penetration, and DA:NE selectivity, and adds σ1 activity. (3) N-ethyl/N-propyl progressively reduce DA release while sparing 5-HT release, biasing the profile toward entactogen. (4) Ring substitution at the 4-position controls SERT engagement: 4-F is intermediate (DA>5-HT, EC50 200 vs 730 nM, Nagai PMID 17223101), 4-Cl is fully SERT-shifted and neurotoxic, 4-Br is similar to 4-Cl, 4-I likewise; 4-methyl gives p-toluidine analogues with SERT shift; 4-methylthio (4-MTA) and 4-methoxy (PMA) are SERT-dominant and add MAO-A inhibition. (5) 2-halogen retains DA selectivity (2-FA EC50 DA ~33 nM, SERT >10 µM — Wee PMID 15914673). (6) 3,4-methylenedioxy makes entactogens (MDMA family — covered elsewhere). (7) β-hydroxyl (→ ephedrine, norephedrine, cathinone family) reduces lipophilicity and CNS penetration ~10×, weakens DA release more than NE release, eliminates TAAR1 efficacy. (8) Beta-keto (→ cathinones) similarly reduces CNS penetration but is metabolised to β-hydroxy. (9) Oxazoline ring (→ aminorex family) gives long-duration releasers with 5-HT2B liability (aminorex caused PPH epidemic 1965–1972). (10) Para-methoxy specifically gives PMA — slow-onset, MAOI-active, deadly (DOI:10.1038/s41573-019-0049-9).

class_name: Cathinones (β-keto phenethylamine stimulants; split into substrate-releasers and pure pyrrolidinophenone reuptake-inhibitors)
shared_mechanism: Synthetic cathinones share the β-ketoamphetamine core and act on monoamine transporters (DAT, NET, SERT), but the class splits sharply into two functional sub-classes based on N-substituent. (1) Primary/N-methyl/N-ethyl cathinones (cathinone, methcathinone, mephedrone, methylone, ethylone, butylone) are SUBSTRATES that produce reverse transport ('release'), analogous to amphetamines but ~10× less CNS-penetrant because the β-keto increases polarity. (2) Pyrrolidinophenones (α-PVP, MDPV, α-PHP, α-PiHP, naphyrone, MDPBP, MDPPP) cannot act as substrates because the bulky pyrrolidine N-substituent prevents the transporter from translocating the molecule across the membrane — they are PURE CATECHOLAMINE REUPTAKE INHIBITORS at sub-nanomolar to low-nanomolar potency at DAT/NET, with little to no SERT activity. The β-keto group at the α-carbon also makes cathinones POOR TAAR1 ligands (negligible agonism at hTAAR1 in Simmler 2016, pmid:26791601) because the carbonyl forces a non-planar geometry that breaks the TAAR1 binding pose. Loss of TAAR1's natural feedback braking on dopamine neuron firing is widely believed to underlie cathinones' higher psychosis risk versus amphetamines.
shared_pk_summary: Cathinones are well absorbed by intranasal/insufflation and oral routes; oral bioavailability is typically lower than amphetamines (mephedrone F ~10% in rats, suggesting first-pass metabolism). Half-lives are short for releaser-type cathinones (mephedrone ~2 h, methylone ~6 h, cathinone ~1.5 h) but longer for MDPV (terminal ~80–100 min in rats but with tissue accumulation extending pharmacodynamic effects; human estimates 4–8 h). Primary metabolism is hepatic, dominated by CYP2D6 for N-demethylation (mephedrone, methcathinone, methylone), with CYP2B6, CYP1A2, CYP2C19 contributing minor pathways. MDPV and pyrrolidinophenones undergo O-demethylenation by CYP1A2/CYP2D6/CYP2C19 followed by catechol-O-methylation by COMT, then glucuronidation. β-keto reduction yields cathine/norephedrine analogues with reduced activity. Plasma protein binding is modest (mephedrone ~22%). Vd is large for the lipophilic pyrrolidinophenones, particularly MDPV which shows tissue accumulation that explains its long-tail effects.
shared_safety: (1) HYPERTHERMIA — a class-defining hazard, multifactorial as with amphetamines, but worsened by the loss of TAAR1 feedback (no autoinhibition of DA firing). (2) SYMPATHETIC CRISIS — extreme HR/BP elevations; MDPV particularly cardiotoxic, with direct hERG and KCNQ1 block at low-μM concentrations (Tarapoulouzi 2024, DOI:10.3390/ijms27010059). (3) PSYCHOSIS AND COMPULSIVE REDOSING — the pyrrolidinophenones (MDPV, α-PVP, α-PHP) have especially severe compulsive-redosing liability because they are sub-nM DAT inhibitors with no release component, no autoreceptor activation from released DA, and no TAAR1 brake — this 'pure DAT slam-cocaine on steroids' profile drives flakka/bath-salts-style psychosis. (4) SEROTONERGIC NEUROTOXICITY RISK — para-halogenated cathinones (4-CMC/clephedrone, 4-CEC, brephedrone, 4F-MABP) are structural analogues of PCMA/PBA, raising a serotonergic axonal neurotoxicity concern; recent in vitro studies show oxidative-stress cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y but classical 5-HT terminal damage in vivo has not been firmly demonstrated yet (Wojcieszak 2020, DOI:10.1007/s12640-020-00227-8). (5) RHABDOMYOLYSIS, HYPONATREMIA (water-loading with SERT-active congeners), DIC, and acute kidney injury all reported. (6) FATALITIES — α-PVP, MDPV, 4-CMC, ephylone (N-ethylpentylone), eutylone, pentylone all have documented fatality clusters.
sar_summary: Core SAR axes for cathinones: (1) β-KETONE is the defining feature — adds polarity, reduces CNS penetration ~10× versus matched amphetamine, eliminates TAAR1 agonism. β-keto is reduced in vivo to β-hydroxy (cathine-like), an active metabolite. (2) N-SUBSTITUENT controls functional mechanism: H, CH3, C2H5 → substrate/releaser; PYRROLIDINE → pure reuptake inhibitor (cannot be transported). (3) α-ALKYL CHAIN LENGTH: methyl (mephedrone/methcathinone) gives ~equipotent DA/NE/5-HT release; ethyl (buphedrone) shifts toward DA selectivity and increases potency; propyl (pentedrone), butyl (hexedrone) progressively boost DAT potency at the cost of SERT. (4) RING SUBSTITUENT controls SERT engagement: unsubstituted gives DA-selective; 3-methyl (3-MMC) is still DAT-preferring; 4-methyl (mephedrone) shifts toward balanced DA/5-HT release; 4-methylenedioxy (methylone, MDPV) further increases SERT engagement for the substrates while killing SERT activity for the pyrrolidinophenones. 4-halogen (4-CMC/4-FMC/4-BMC/4F-MABP) mimics the SERT-shift of para-halogenated amphetamines and raises a serotonergic-neurotoxicity flag by analogy to PCA/4-CA. (5) AROMATIC EXTENSION — naphthyl (naphyrone) re-introduces SERT activity to the pyrrolidinophenone scaffold via a larger aromatic surface. (6) For pyrrolidinophenones, increasing α-alkyl chain from propyl (MDPPP, α-PPP) → butyl (MDPBP, α-PBP) → pentyl (MDPV, α-PVP) → hexyl (α-PHP, α-PiHP) monotonically increases DAT potency and lipophilicity, with α-PVP and α-PHP being the most potent pure DAT blockers in the class (sub-30-nM IC50).

class_name: Dopamine transporter (DAT) inhibitors — cocaine-like / phenidate-like / NDRI
shared_mechanism: Block reuptake of DA (+/- NE +/- 5-HT) at the orthosteric site of SLC6A3 (DAT). The functional split that matters clinically is binding kinetics and DAT conformation, not chemical scaffold: 'cocaine-like' inhibitors (cocaine, methylphenidate, RTI-150, WIN-35,428, JJC8-088) stabilise DAT in an outward-open conformation, exhibit fast association/dissociation, and produce euphoria; 'atypical' DAT inhibitors (modafinil, JJC8-091, JHW-007, AHN-1055, vanoxerine, CE-123) stabilise an inward-occluded conformation, exhibit slow binding/dissociation, achieve partial DAT occupancy at therapeutic doses, and lack abuse liability. NDRIs (bupropion, methylphenidate, mazindol, atomoxetine via NE→DA spillover) hit both NET and DAT; PFC dopamine clearance is NET-dominated, so NDRI gives strong cognitive enhancement without striatal DA spike — better tolerability/cardiovascular profile depends on net DAT/NET ratio.
shared_pk_summary: Cocaine: hepatic + plasma BChE + CES1 hydrolysis; t1/2 ~1 h (intranasal/IV) — fast in/out is the key abuse parameter. Methylphenidate and ester homologues: CES1 stereoselective hydrolysis (l-MPH cleared 5-10x faster than d-MPH; explains 22% vs 5% bioavailability respectively); CES1 G143E reduces clearance. Bupropion: CYP2B6→hydroxybupropion (active, NET-selective, 4-7x parent plasma); CYP2B6*6 reduces metabolite. Atomoxetine: CYP2D6 — PMs have 10x AUC, 5x Cmax, t1/2 21.6h vs 5.2h EM. Modafinil: hepatic amidase + CYP3A4/5; long t1/2 ~15h; weak CYP3A4 inducer (reduces oral contraceptive efficacy), weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. Lisdexamfetamine and serdexmethylphenidate: prodrugs (RBC aminopeptidases for LDX; gut hydrolysis for SDX) — rate-limited bioactivation deflates IV/IN abuse routes.
shared_safety: hERG block + Nav1.5 block → arrhythmia, sudden cardiac death (cocaine prototype; cocaethylene 4x worse). Atypical DAT inhibitors with sigma binding (JHW-007) and modafinil analogs (JJC8-088 IC50 0.13 µM at hERG) carry intrinsic hERG risk. Bupropion lowers seizure threshold (dose-dependent; 0.4% at ≤450 mg/day). All abused stimulants risk sympathomimetic crisis, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis at supratherapeutic doses. CES1 G143E and BChE deficiency are genetic risk factors for cocaine/MPH toxicity. CYP3A4 induction (modafinil/armodafinil) → oral contraceptive failure, reduced AUC of co-administered substrates (encorafenib, triazolam, ethinyl estradiol).
sar_summary: Cocaine scaffold: replacing C3 benzoyloxy with phenyl (phenyltropanes) → markedly higher DAT affinity (WIN-35,428 Kd 16 nM vs cocaine 300 nM) and slower dissociation; 4-iodo (RTI-55) adds SERT; 4-chloro phenyl ester (RTI-113) maximises DAT selectivity (1500x vs NET); N-substitution of benztropine scaffold from methyl→butyl shifts from cocaine-like (benztropine) to atypical/non-reinforcing (JHW-007, AHN-1055). Methylphenidate scaffold: ester chain length (Me→Et→iPr→Pr) shifts NET→DAT selectivity (d-MPH NET Ki 38 nM vs d-EPH NET Ki 3700 nM); 3,4-dichloro on phenyl (3,4-CTMP) gives 7-fold potency boost + esterase resistance → long duration. Modafinil scaffold: bis-4-fluoro (flmodafinil) boosts DAT affinity ~4x and abolishes CYP induction; small N-substituent changes in JJC8-088 vs -091 series produce activity cliff between cocaine-like and atypical profile (DAT conformation determined by single methyl difference). Phenylmorpholine releasers (phenmetrazine): 3-fluoro, 3-chloro maintain NE/DA releaser profile; 4-methyl or 3,4-methylenedioxy add 5-HT release → MDMA-like entactogen profile.

class_name: Phenyltropanes (RTI series, WIN-35,428) — cocaine-derived DAT-selective inhibitors
shared_mechanism: Tropane scaffold of cocaine with the C3 benzoyloxy ester replaced by a phenyl ring (no oxygen at C3-aryl junction); C2 carbomethoxy retained. Removes the metabolically labile ester bond → much longer half-life and slower brain entry than cocaine. Binds DAT orthosteric site competitively with cocaine; most phenyltropanes are cocaine-like (outward-facing conformation, fast on/off) but with longer duration of action because the ester is replaced by a non-hydrolysable bond. SAR: 4-aryl substituent dictates DAT selectivity (4-F = WIN-35,428 highest selectivity for DAT; 4-I = RTI-55 adds SERT; 4-Me = RTI-150). C2 substituent dictates duration (C2 phenyl ester = RTI-113 long-acting).
shared_pk_summary: Generally lipophilic with slow brain entry (vs cocaine) and long half-lives (hours to days); ester hydrolysis is the main clearance pathway when C2 carbomethoxy is retained, but C2 modifications (esters, amides) can produce very long elimination. Used primarily as PET/SPECT radioligands (WIN-35,428 [11C], β-CIT/RTI-55 [123I]) in human DAT imaging — slow brain kinetics is desirable for imaging but argues against therapeutic translation in pure form.
shared_safety: Phenyltropanes inherit cocaine's cardiovascular off-targets (hERG, Nav1.5) to varying degrees; specific human data sparse since most are research tools. RTI-113 and others have been tested in primate self-administration with high reinforcing efficacy, but slower onset reduces (rather than eliminates) abuse liability. Atypical phenyltropanes (those stabilising occluded DAT conformation) like indatraline have lower abuse liability.
sar_summary: C3-aryl 4-position controls selectivity: H ~ cocaine; F → DAT-selective (WIN-35,428); I → adds SERT (RTI-55); Me → cocaine-like (RTI-150); 3,4-Cl2 → high potency. C2 substituent controls duration: methyl ester (cocaine) hydrolysed by esterases (t1/2 min); phenyl ester (RTI-113) and amides resist hydrolysis (t1/2 hours). N8 substituent (methyl→nor or larger groups) modulates affinity and kinetics: nor- generally less potent; larger N-substituents can flip from cocaine-like to atypical.

class_name: Atypical DAT inhibitors — modafinil-derived (JJC, CE, SoRI series)
shared_mechanism: Diphenylmethyl-sulfinyl-acetamide scaffold (modafinil) and ring-expanded/N-substituted variants. Mechanism distinct from cocaine: at the DAT, these compounds stabilise inward-facing or occluded conformations (rather than outward-open) and exhibit SLOW association and dissociation kinetics. Slow kinetics → blunted reinforcement (the dopaminergic spike does not have sharp onset) → low abuse liability. Some (JJC8-088 specifically) violate this rule by stabilising outward-open, demonstrating the conformation hypothesis: modafinil-derived chemistry can produce both atypical and cocaine-like profiles depending on subtle N- and aryl-substituent choices (activity cliff). Modafinil parent additionally activates orexin/hypocretin neurons in lateral hypothalamus → histamine TMN → wakefulness (DAT inhibition alone is insufficient to explain its eugeroic profile at clinical doses).
shared_pk_summary: Modafinil: oral t1/2 ~12-15h (racemate); armodafinil 10-15h; bioavailability high (~80%); CYP3A4/5 + amidase metabolism to inactive sulfone (t1/2 40h) and acid (t1/2 7h). Modafinil is weak CYP3A4 inducer and weak CYP2C19 inhibitor; flmodafinil is reportedly NOT a CYP inducer (key advantage). Adrafinil prodrug hepatically converted to modafinil (~50%) but carries additional hepatotoxicity from hydroxamic acid moiety. Atypical research compounds (JJC, CE-123) have very long half-lives by design to maintain slow brain kinetics.
shared_safety: Major concern: hERG block (JJC8-088 IC50 0.13 µM; medchem effort to reduce). Modafinil: rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome / DRESS (FDA label warns), CYP3A4 induction → contraceptive failure. Vanoxerine: multi-channel cardiac block (hERG IC50 0.84 nM, Nav1.5, Cav1.2) but minimal APD prolongation — paradoxically antiarrhythmic. Atypical DAT profile generally low abuse liability — proposed mechanism for stimulant use disorder treatment.
sar_summary: Single N-substituent change (e.g. JJC8-088 vs -091) flips conformational preference and abuse-likability: this is the 'activity cliff'. Adding fluorines to diphenyl rings (flmodafinil vs modafinil) increases DAT affinity ~4x without changing atypical character and removes CYP induction. Hydroxamic acid moiety (adrafinil, fladrafinil) confers hepatotoxicity. CE-123 series replaces sulfinyl with thio/sulfonyl groups to tune selectivity.

class_name: Atypical DAT inhibitors — N-substituted benztropines (AHN, JHW series)
shared_mechanism: Tropane-diphenylmethylether scaffold of benztropine. Despite high DAT affinity (Ki single-digit nM), N-substituent (especially N-butyl, JHW-007) yields atypical DAT inhibitor profile: slow onset, partial DAT occupancy at high doses, no cocaine-like reinforcement, blocks (rather than substitutes for) cocaine in self-administration and discrimination. Mechanism: stabilises DAT in inward-occluded conformation. Many in this series additionally bind sigma-1 and sigma-2 receptors at therapeutic concentrations, which may contribute to anti-cocaine effects. Slow binding kinetics + DAT-independent striatal binding sites (residual binding in DAT-knockout mice) are signatures of the class.
shared_pk_summary: Highly lipophilic → slow brain entry and prolonged half-lives. Limited human PK published. Benztropine itself: oral, t1/2 ~16h; N-substituted analogues lipophilicity-dependent.
shared_safety: Inherited from benztropine: anticholinergic burden (M1, M2 muscarinic antagonism — dry mouth, urinary retention, cognitive impairment in elderly); H1 antihistamine (sedation). Sigma-1 antagonism may have unknown long-term consequences. Lower abuse liability is the chief advantage.
sar_summary: N-methyl (benztropine, AHN-1055) → modest DAT affinity, partial cocaine-like profile. N-butyl/longer (JHW-007) → atypical, non-reinforcing, cocaine-antagonist profile. Bis-(4-fluoro) on diphenyl improves DAT selectivity. Removing tropane methyl yields nor-analogues with altered conformational preference at DAT.

class_name: Phenylmorpholine substrate-type monoamine releasers (phenmetrazine and analogues)
shared_mechanism: Substituted phenylmorpholine scaffold. Acts as substrate at DAT and NET — taken up via transporter, then displaces vesicular monoamines (via VMAT2 substrate competition / weak-base trapping) → reverse transport of DA and NE into synapse (efflux). Distinct from cocaine-class uptake blockers — releaser pharmacology produces stronger and more sustained DA/NE rise. Aryl-ring substitution dictates serotonergic add-on: parent phenmetrazine essentially NE/DA-selective (negligible SERT); 4-methyl (4-MPM) and 3,4-methylenedioxy (MDPM) shift toward 5-HT releaser activity (MDMA-like entactogen profile).
shared_pk_summary: Phenmetrazine: oral t1/2 ~8h. Phendimetrazine (N-methyl analogue): inactive prodrug, slow CYP N-demethylation to phenmetrazine — flatter PK profile reduces abuse liability vs phenmetrazine itself. Fluorinated analogues (3-FPM) and Cl-substituted (3-CPM) have variable PK; halogenation typically extends duration via metabolic stabilisation.
shared_safety: Releaser pharmacology produces stronger sympathomimetic load than uptake-blocker class — hypertension, tachycardia, vasoconstriction (3-FPM AKI + critical limb ischemia case reports). MDMA-like analogues (4-MPM) add serotonin syndrome risk and 5-HT2B-mediated valvulopathy concern with chronic use.
sar_summary: Halogen at C3 (F, Cl) maintains NE/DA selectivity and modestly potentiates DAT release. Halogen at C4 (4-F) similar. C4 methyl or 3,4-methylenedioxy adds substantial SERT releaser activity → MDMA-like profile. N-methylation (phendimetrazine) abolishes activity, generating slow-release prodrug of demethylated form (phenmetrazine).

class_name: Eugeroic afinils (modafinil, adrafinil, fladrafinil, hydrafinil, etc.)
shared_mechanism: Predominant clinically active member is modafinil. Mechanism is multimodal: (1) weak DAT inhibition (modafinil DAT Ki ~4 µM; PET shows 50% striatal DAT occupancy at 200-400 mg in humans), (2) ORE EXIN/hypocretin neuron activation in lateral hypothalamus (modafinil increases orexin neuron c-Fos), (3) downstream histaminergic TMN activation (modafinil-induced wakefulness requires intact histamine neurons), (4) modest glutamate↑ and GABA↓ in cortical networks. Adrafinil is hepatic prodrug of modafinil; fladrafinil is bis-fluoro adrafinil; flmodafinil/bisfluoromodafinil is bis-fluoro modafinil (improved DAT affinity, no CYP induction); hydrafinil is structurally unrelated fluorenol with weak/poorly characterised mechanism.
shared_pk_summary: Modafinil: oral F ~80%, t1/2 12-15h, Tmax 2h, protein binding 60%. Metabolised CYP3A4/5 + hepatic amidase to inactive sulfone (t1/2 40h) and acid (t1/2 7h). Weak CYP3A4 inducer (clinically relevant for hormonal contraceptives, triazolam, encorafenib), weak CYP2C19 inhibitor (warfarin, omeprazole). Armodafinil (R-enantiomer): t1/2 ~15h (slightly longer than racemate because R-eutomer clears slower than S). Adrafinil: prodrug t1/2 ~1h before conversion to modafinil; adds hepatotoxicity (LFT elevation; French market withdrawal 2011).
shared_safety: Rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome, DRESS, toxic epidermal necrolysis (FDA boxed-warning class). CYP3A4 induction → contraceptive failure. Adrafinil/fladrafinil class hepatotoxicity (hydroxamic acid moiety). Generally low abuse liability — but reinforcing in vulnerable populations; classified US Schedule IV.
sar_summary: Bis-4-fluoro on diphenyl (flmodafinil, fladrafinil) increases DAT affinity ~4x and removes CYP3A4 induction. Hydroxamic acid (adrafinil, fladrafinil) → hepatotoxicity. Sulfinyl→sulfonyl (modafinil sulfone): inactive. Acetamide→acetic acid (modafinil acid): inactive. R-enantiomer of modafinil is the eutomer (slower clearance, similar potency).

class_name: Selective NE reuptake inhibitors (atomoxetine, viloxazine)
shared_mechanism: Block NET (SLC6A2) with high selectivity over DAT and SERT. In prefrontal cortex, NET co-transports BOTH NE and DA (because PFC has low DAT density), so selective NET inhibition raises PFC DA without striatal DA spike → cognitive enhancement without abuse liability. No reinforcement, no euphoria. Viloxazine adds serotonergic activity (5-HT2C partial agonism, 5-HT2B/2C/7 antagonism) — differentiates from atomoxetine. Both used in ADHD as non-stimulant alternatives.
shared_pk_summary: Atomoxetine: oral F 63% (EM) / 94% (CYP2D6 PM); t1/2 5.2h EM / 21.6h PM (10x AUC, 5x Cmax); protein binding 98% (albumin). CYP2D6 primary; CYP2C19 minor. Viloxazine ER: t1/2 7h, Tmax 5h, protein binding 76%; UGT1A9/UGT2B15 primary; CYP2D6 minor (PMs have only 21-26% increase, no dose adjust). Viloxazine is strong CYP1A2 inhibitor (caffeine, theophylline AUC doubled).
shared_safety: Atomoxetine: rare hepatic injury (boxed warning), modest QT prolongation in PMs, suicidality concern (FDA boxed warning, pediatric). Viloxazine: CYP1A2 interactions (caffeine, theophylline, melatonin, clozapine). Both: dry mouth, decreased appetite, insomnia common; no significant abuse liability.
sar_summary: Phenoxypropylamine (atomoxetine) and morpholine (viloxazine) scaffolds. CYP2D6 stereoselective metabolism (atomoxetine R-isomer hydroxylated faster than S). NET selectivity over DAT/SERT 290-fold (atomoxetine) to 100-fold (viloxazine) — high enough to avoid abuse.

class_name: Serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitors (SNDRIs / triple reuptake inhibitors)
shared_mechanism: Simultaneous inhibition of SERT, NET, and DAT at the orthosteric sites. Designed for major depression with the theory that DA component would address anhedonia/motivation deficit unmet by SSRIs/SNRIs. Most programs failed because hitting DAT at antidepressant doses creates abuse liability (e.g., dasotraline) or hERG/cardiovascular issues. Dasotraline succeeded by extreme PK flattening (t1/2 47-77h → infusion-like exposure, no peak-trough abuse pattern) but was discontinued for commercial reasons. Indatraline and brasofensine are classic research-grade SNDRIs.
shared_pk_summary: Variable; medicinal-chemistry effort focused on extending half-life to avoid peak abuse liability. Dasotraline t1/2 47-77h; brasofensine and indatraline shorter. Most metabolised by hepatic CYPs.
shared_safety: DAT activity drives abuse liability if PK is sharp. Pridefine: noncompetitive uptake inhibition mode (mechanistic curiosity). Hypertension/tachycardia from NE + DA effects. Serotonin syndrome risk if combined with SSRIs/MAOIs. Hepatic concerns with several compounds.
sar_summary: Phenyltropane (brasofensine), aminoindane (indatraline, dasotraline), pyrroloisoquinoline (JNJ-7925476), pyrrolidine (pridefine). Within each scaffold, halogen substitution on aryl moiety tunes SERT vs DAT vs NET potency ratios. Dasotraline (1R,4S-aminotetralin) directly derived from tametraline → sertraline series with stereochemistry tuned for SNDRI rather than SSRI profile.
